functions.name: readSkeletonData_slotTimelines

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_slotTimelines(Json* slotMap, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw, void* parser_raw)
abi.slotMap: first node of the "slots" JSON child list; parent spill [sp+0x2c], loaded 0x28d520, advanced 0x28d62c..0x28d638
abi.return: 1 = fall through to the bones block at 0x28d640; 0 = left through an out-of-block error path (see quirks)

functions.semantics: Per slot node: slotIndex = real spSkeletonData_findSlotIndex(data, slotMap->name@+0x1c) (0x28d524..0x28d52c). slotIndex == -1 (cmn r0,#1 @0x28d530) branches to 0x28ea10 ("Slot not found: ", outside this module). Otherwise timelineJson = slotMap->child (+0x4, 0x28d540); per timeline node the type text is timelineJson->name (+0x1c, 0x28d54c) and the dispatch is a two-step strcmp chain: "color" -> B8 (beq 0x28d560), else "attachment" -> B5 attachment branch, else bne 0x28da18 (E1). Back edges: 0x28d620 timelineJson = timelineJson->next / 0x28d62c slotMap = slotMap->next.

name.role: kept in r7 for the attachment frame read

time.role: kept in r6 for the attachment frame read

frame_index_source.finding: B5/B8 contain no `mov r5,#0`; the dispatch reuses r5 for the strcmp result (0x28d55c and 0x28d570 `subs r5,r0,#0`) and each branch is entered only on the matching (== 0) comparison, so every frame loop starts at index 0 by construction.
frame_index_source.consequence: the frame index never carries across timelines or slots; after the slots block r5 is dead (B6b re-clears it at 0x28d754)
frame_index_source.census_relation: not covered by animations_segment_map.md; consistent with §5.3's loop table

quirks: 0x28d538 beq 0x28ea10: the -1 slot index leaves this module. That block ("Slot not found: ") is deliberately not reconstructed here; the function only reports the branch through its return value.
the slot name is read from the JSON member key (+0x1c), never from a "name" key: there is no Json_getString in the lookup path
no allocation of any kind happens in B5 outside the timeline creators
a slot node with no children skips to the next slot (0x28d544/0x28d548)

functions.name: readSkeletonData_attachmentTimeline
functions.address_range: 0x28d578-0x28d61c (attachment branch of B5, 42 insns; entry reached from 0x28d574 bne fall-through)

abi.signature: void readSkeletonData_attachmentTimeline(Json* timelineJson, void* animation_raw, int slotIndex)
calls: spAttachmentTimeline_setFrame(timeline, index, time, name) -> 0x282c1c (synthetic boundary; r0..r3)

functions.semantics: timeline = spAttachmentTimeline_create(declared frame count from Json+0x0c) (0x28d578/0x28d57c); timeline->slotIndex (+0x10) = slotIndex (0x28d590); frame = timelineJson->child (0x28d580). Per frame: name_node = Json_getItem(frame,"name") (0x28d598..0x28d5a0), time = Json_getFloat(frame,"time",0) (0x28d5a4..0x28d5b4), kind = name_node->unk_08 (0x28d5b8), argument name = (kind == 2) ? NULL : name_node->string_value (0x28d5c4..0x28d5cc), spAttachmentTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, name) (0x28d5d0..0x28d5d8), frame = frame->next (0x28d5dc). Loop condition is the frame child list (0x28d5e0/0x28d5e4), never the declared count.
functions.tail: 0x28d5e8..0x28d61c: count = animation->timelineCount(+0x08); duration = animation->duration(+0x04); timelines = animation->timelines(+0x0c); animation->timelineCount = count + 1; timelines[count] = timeline; last = frames[declared-1] with a ONE-float frame stride (frames at timeline+0x0c, 0x28d604 `add r3,r3,r2,lsl#2` then `vldr s15,[r3,#-4]`); animation->duration = (duration > last) ? duration : last (vcmpe.f32 + vmovgt.f32 at 0x28d610/0x28d618).

field_offsets.spAttachmentTimeline+0x0c: float* frames, one time float per frame (real creator 0x282bf8)

quirks: the attachment-name discriminator is the Json node's +0x08 word compared with 2: the value 2 (the parser's 'false' kind) yields a NULL name, every other kind forwards +0x10 verbatim. This is not the stock `name ? name->valueString : 0` shape and its intent cannot be derived from this block.
there is no NULL guard on the Json_getItem(frame,"name") result before 0x28d5b8 `ldr r3,[r10,#0x8]`: a frame without a "name" member faults in the original
the frame loop is driven by the child list while the tail indexes frames[declared-1]; a declared count larger than the child count reads never-written slots, a declared count of 0 indexes frames[-1]

functions.name: readSkeletonData_colorTimeline

abi.signature: void readSkeletonData_colorTimeline(Json* timelineJson, void* animation_raw, int slotIndex)
calls: spColorTimeline_setFrame(timeline, i, time, r, g, b, a) -> 0x282b54 (synthetic boundary; r0,r1,r2,r3,[sp],[sp+4],[sp+8])

functions.semantics: timeline = spColorTimeline_create(declared count) (0x28d8dc/0x28d8e0); timeline->slotIndex (+0x14, NOT +0x10) = slotIndex (0x28d8f4); frame = timelineJson->child. Per frame: color = Json_getString(frame,"color",0) (0x28d920..0x28d92c); time = Json_getFloat(frame,"time",0) (0x28d930..0x28d940); r = toColor(color,0), g = toColor(color,1), b = toColor(color,2), a = toColor(color,3) in that order (0x28d944..0x28d980); spColorTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, r, g, b, a) (0x28d984..0x28d9a0); readCurve(frame, timeline, frameIndex) with the same index (0x28d9a4..0x28d9b0); frame = frame->next (0x28d9b4); frameIndex++ (0x28d9b8).
functions.tail: 0x28d9d4..0x28da10: declared = Json+0x0c; duration = animation->duration; count = animation->timelineCount; timelines = animation->timelines; wordIndex = (declared-1)*5 (0x28d9e4 sub, 0x28d9f0 `add r2,r2,r2,lsl#2`); animation->timelineCount = count+1; timelines[count] = timeline; last = frames[wordIndex] (frames at +0x10, 0x28d9f8/0x28d9fc); animation->duration = (duration > last) ? duration : last (0x28da04..0x28da10). Then b 0x28d620 (0x28da14) returns to the timeline loop.

hex_color_channel.shape: the JSON "color" value is an EIGHT-character hex STRING read with Json_getString; there is no rgba array read anywhere in this family
hex_color_channel.component_order: toColor(value,0)=r, 1=g, 2=b, 3=a; the original calls them in that order and spills r first (vstr s0,[sp,#0x10]) then keeps g in s17 and b in s16
hex_color_channel.validation_in_b8: none. A missing key reaches toColor(NULL,.) and a malformed string reaches all four components unmodified; malformed input is only rejected inside toColor (length != 8 -> -1.0f, strtoul end != 0 -> -1.0f)
hex_color_channel.stock_divergence: confirmed: this build does not accept the stock `"color":[r,g,b,a]` array form (census §2.9 / §7 item 3, now closed)

field_offsets.spColorTimeline+0x08: float* curves, (frameCount-1)*19 floats (_spCurveTimeline_init 0x281700/0x281708/0x281710); this is readCurve's setStepped index stride, NOT a frame count
field_offsets.spColorTimeline+0x10: float* frames, FIVE floats per frame time,r,g,b,a (_spBaseTimeline_create 0x282a78; real setFrame 0x282b58)

quirks: the color and attachment timelines keep slotIndex at DIFFERENT offsets (+0x14 vs +0x10) because only the attachment record has the names table at +0x14
readCurve is called with the same 0-based frame index and the same timeline pointer that setFrame received, after setFrame returns
no allocation in B8/B8b outside the creator

calls: _spSkeletonJson_setError(parser, NULL, "Invalid timeline type for a slot: ", type) -> 0x28b784 (real; console vcall + line-90 copy)

functions.semantics: type = timelineJson->name (+0x1c, 0x28da34) is captured first, then spAnimation_dispose(animation) (0x28da28), then _spSkeletonJson_setError(parser, 0, "Invalid timeline type for a slot: ", type) (0x28da30..0x28da40), then spSkeletonData_dispose(data) (0x28da44..0x28da48), then return 0 (0x28da4c) which the parent turns into a NULL return at 0x28bdcc.

error_text.literal: Invalid timeline type for a slot:
error_text.formatted_example: Invalid timeline type for a slot: rotate

quirks: the setError json argument is r1 = 0 (0x28da38 mov r1,#0), so unlike the slots-bone error at 0x28bdc4 the root Json tree is NOT disposed here
the offending text is the timeline node's JSON member key, not a string value
the animation is disposed BEFORE the error is formatted, and the half-built skeleton data AFTER it: the order is observable through the free roster
spAnimation_dispose walks the already-published timelines through spTimeline_dispose ([[self+4]+4]) before freeing the table and the record

open: Why the attachment frame treats a node whose +0x08 word is 2 (the parser's 'false' kind) as 'no attachment name' is not derivable from B5; the branch is reconstructed literally.

declared frame count == 0 with no children still reaches the publish tail and indexes frames[-1] (attachment) / frames[-5] (color). The fixture never drives that combination; the original's behaviour there is not asserted.

A frame without a "name" key (attachment) or without a "color" key (color) faults in the original (no NULL guard at 0x28d5b8 / at the toColor call). Not reproducible in the fixture without a fault probe.
toColor's own contract (8-character length check, strtoul, signed VCVT) belongs to c/spine_color; B8 adds no validation of its own.
The bodies of the four timeline entry points remain unrecovered: only their argument record and the store shape the tails depend on are modelled.
What the parent does with the -1 slot index (0x28ea10 "Slot not found: " block) is outside these four blocks.
No skeleton JSON asset exists in this tree, so how many slot timelines the shipped data actually uses is unknown.

census_cross_check.hex_color: §2.9's claim (Json_getString + 0x28b680 x4, no rgba array) confirmed instruction by instruction
census_cross_check.correction_1: §6 calls B8b the 'color/attachment common tail'. It is not shared code: B5 carries its own inline copy at 0x28d5e8 that reads frames at +0x0c with a one-float stride, while B8b reads +0x10 with a five-float stride. Only the shape (publish + max-duration) is common.
census_cross_check.correction_2: §6's B8b note 'readCurve 调用点 0x28d9b0 一带' places that call inside B8's address range (0x28d9b0 < 0x28d9d4); B8b itself contains no readCurve call.
census_cross_check.addition_1: the slot family's frame index comes from the dispatch strcmp result in r5 (0x28d55c/0x28d570), which is why no zero-initialisation appears in B5/B8 (§9's stack-slot open item does not cover it).
census_cross_check.addition_2: color stores slotIndex at +0x14 and attachment at +0x10; §6/§7 do not record either offset.
census_cross_check.addition_3: E1 passes json = NULL to setError (0x28da38), so the root tree is not disposed on this path; §5.4 only lists the call order.
census_cross_check.addition_4: the two slot timeline records disagree at +0x08: spAttachmentTimeline stores frameCount there (0x282bd8), spColorTimeline stores the (frameCount-1)*19 curves array (_spCurveTimeline_init 0x281710). The tails consequently read frames from +0x0c and +0x10 respectively.
